body:
Just linking to the original issue reported here https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/issues/1415

And a little of context

> based on my limited testing, the problem seems to start when treesitter in the neovim was upgraded to 0.19.5 on 6/11/21

For reference, that commit updated tree-sitter from
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/commit/89e1157a299596f3ce2155ba9fd69d5e2c03d3e6
to
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/commit/6ed42747a4e0faee9b65edbbacc86ed0caeae05c

If someone wanted to bisect this (manually, I'm afraid) by replacing the commit ID (and hash) in
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/24e0c16fd6cb33a399772330cb80dfa4c1306284/third-party/CMakeLists.txt#L213-L214
and rebuilding to see which commit between the two introduced the performance regression, that would be helpful.
I can take a shot at this, but how is the sha256 for line 214 generated?

Well, the "easy" way is to just omit it and check the error message for the expected hash ;)

Less facetiously: This is the hash of the _zip file_ containing the repo at that commit. You could also download the zip and do `shasum -a 256 tree-sitterXXXX.zip`.
I can also mess with it after work @mizlan, let me know how it goes for you.
The unbearable lag also exists in my tex files.
Is it solved by building from the old commit?

> If someone wanted to bisect this (manually, I'm afraid) by replacing the commit ID (and hash) in

```
78010722a49ed6224c773c22b0d25a8c9fbde584 is the first bad commit
commit 78010722a49ed6224c773c22b0d25a8c9fbde584
Author: Douglas Creager <dcreager@dcreager.net>
Date:   Thu May 13 15:38:11 2021 -0400

    query: Allow unlimited pending matches
    
    Well, not completely unlimited — we're still using a 16-bit counter to
    keep track of them.  But we longer have a static maximum of 32 pending
    matches when executing a query.

 cli/src/tests/query_test.rs |  4 +++
 lib/src/query.c             | 72 ++++++++++++++++++---------------------------
 2 files changed, 33 insertions(+), 43 deletions(-)
```

I made a script for this https://gist.github.com/mizlan/50ea7fadbc9b016eae87d6522cb771ab that may be useful in the future.

For the record, that is https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/commit/78010722a49ed6224c773c22b0d25a8c9fbde584

A later commit (https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/commit/cd96552448a6e0d4eb27fc54b27cb5130c4b6f76) introduced a configurable match limit via `ts_query_cursor_set_match_limit`  that may be used to set it back to the old default of 32 (as is done in their test).

Does that answer the question around:

>and rebuilding to see which commit between the two introduced the performance regression, that would be helpful.

then @clason? And presumably, granted I have _zero_ clue how _Neovim_ interacts with the parsers, the path forward then would be to either specify a value for the parameter with what is pulled in to _Neovim_, or make it exposed to _Neovim_ and defaulted to the old value?

Not sure I'm the best person (more than willing to try though), but I assume the path forward is to either do something like above, or rollback the version pulled in to _Neovim_?

Yes, that answers the question. We'll have to see what to do with this information. Rolling back is not an option since that commit was deliberately pulled in because it fixes other bugs.

(Again, to make this clear: right now there is _zero_ guarantee that tree-sitter is usable for your actual work. Use it _only_ if you like playing early access and want to help find and fix bugs.)

issue.title: Slow tsx and typescript

labels.name: needs information
labels.description: Needs more information or a reproducible scenario

repository.name: nvim-treesitter
repository.description: Nvim Treesitter configurations and abstraction layer

issue.body:
**Describe the bug** TSX and TypeScript files take a noticeably longer time to load than JavaScript files. I have looked at `--startuptime` and `:profile` logs, and even when I delete all default regex-based syntax files loaded for TypeScript by NeoVim, treesitter is slow to load TS / TSX files. I saw on issues like #1082 , people are having the same issue as me. I've seen that it might be due to the newer versions of [tree-sitter](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/issues/973)? **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Install latest versions of NeoVim, treesitter, and nvim-treesitter. 2. Install treesitter parsers for typescript and tsx. 3. Open file and observe slow loading time. 4. Compare with opening JavaScript or JSX files with their respective treesitter parsers. **Expected behavior** Fast loading time, comparable to JSX files. **Output of `:checkhealth nvim_treesitter`**
**Output of `nvim --version`**
**Additional context**

body:
> Is it solved by building from the old commit?

I can confirm that building neovim at `988f88c24e83c37e1dc011e3561fb505ca7b8706` fixes the issue.
@brymer-meneses Do you have linux build? If so can u share it?
